stories.title: Reserve Bank of India launches data center in Bhubaneswar, Odisha
stories.summary: 700-rack facility to support primary data center in Navi Mumbai
stories.content:
The central bank of India has launched a new data center in Odisha.

Over the weekend, India’s Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi, inaugurated the Reserve Bank of India’s newly established Data Centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute in Bhubaneswar, Odisha.

The bank said the new facility “marks a significant milestone in strengthening the technological foundation of India’s financial system.”

Ground was broken on the 18.5-acre development at Info Valley-II in March 2023. According to a presentation shown during the ceremony, the new data center has capacity for 700 racks and will support the bank’s payment processes and systems acting as a backup site to its primary facility in Navi Mumbai.

The site has been certified to Tier IV standards by Uptime. The complex also features 590kW of on-site solar capacity.

Established in 1935, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is the central bank of India. It is headquartered in Mumbai. It has another data center in Kharghar in Navi Mumbai.

Prime Minister Modi described the facility as a reflection of India’s changing approach to governance focused on taking the benefits of economic development to every region and every citizen. He emphasized that a secure banking system needs secure digital infrastructure supported by robust data centers and powerful computing systems, and RBI’s new data center is a critical step in this direction.

stories.title: US$50 bil AI investment: Tanjung Embang identified as strategic location, says Abang Johari
stories.summary: The US$50 billion (RM204 billion) investment announced by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim recently includes strategic plans by a major international company to develop an artificial intelligence (AI) data centre in Tanjung Embang.

sources.name: The Edge Malaysia — data centre search

stories.content:
KUCHING (Oct 26): The US$50 billion (RM204 billion) investment announced by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim recently includes strategic plans by a major international company to develop an artificial intelligence (AI) data centre in Tanjung Embang.

Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg said further details, including the name of the company involved, could not be disclosed at this stage to preserve the confidentiality of the corporate transaction.

“What the prime minister said is true, but it is still at the planning stage. There is indeed a proposal to invest in an AI data centre.

“We cannot disclose the amount for now because it involves a top international company...we cannot reveal its name, but it is indeed there,” he told reporters after officiating at the Sarawak Urban Forum 2.0 here on Monday.

Earlier in his speech, Abang Johari revealed that the prime minister himself had contacted him to enquire about the entry of the world's leading technology investor into Sarawak.

The premier said the international technology giant had chosen Kuching as its investment destination because it views Sarawak as a forward-looking state that is aggressively transitioning towards a new economy.

“The topmost technology company in the world is coming to Kuching. Why? Because they see that we are forward-looking.

“Sarawak is transitioning to a new economy and we have prepared Sarawakians in terms of human capital. We provide free education, and that is why they like it because they know they will have good people to work with them,” he said.

On Saturday, the media reported that the prime minister revealed that a global technology company had chosen Malaysia, including Sarawak and Peninsular Malaysia, for a US$50 billion investment in the AI sector.

stories.title: APDCA outlines policy steps for Asia Pacific data center growth
stories.summary: The Asia-Pacific Data Centre Association (APDCA) released a whitepaper with 10 policy recommendations for governments. It aims to support data center investment while managing infrastructure and resource constraints in the region.
stories.content:
The Asia-Pacific Data Centre Association (APDCA) has released a whitepaper outlining 10 policy recommendations to help governments support data center investment.Titled “Maximizing the Data Center Opportunity — A Playbook for Policymakers,” the document addresses managing infrastructure and resource constraints across the Asia-Pacific region. Key considerations include access to electricity, water, land, and connectivity, alongside predictable investment policies and sufficient infrastructure capacity.Jeremy Deutsch, Chair of APDCA, stated that the playbook offers practical examples for governments. These examples are drawn from the experience of operators building and running data centers in various markets.The whitepaper finds that investments are increasingly mobile. Jurisdictions compete on policy certainty, efficient approvals, and the ability to support sustainable long-term growth.Permitting time and uncertainty associated with approvals are the most common barriers to data center investment, according to the whitepaper. Lengthy, opaque, or poorly coordinated approval processes can delay investment and increase financing costs.The recommendations are grouped into three areas: Plan, Provision, and Partner. These cover demand forecasting, infrastructure planning, investment frameworks, and approval processes. They also include collaboration with industry and communities to develop skills and build public trust.

stories.title: Johor plans to meet DC power demand with 5 GW solar energy by 2031
stories.summary: The Johor government plans to increase its solar energy generation capacity to 5 GW by 2030-31, as the Malaysian state’s growing data center sector continues to demand increasing amounts of electricity. The Johor state government had approved 65 data center projects, with 21 already operational, and expected to consume nearly 1.1 GW of electricity, while […]
stories.content:
The Johor government plans to increase its solar energy generation capacity to 5 GW by 2030-31, as the Malaysian state’s growing data center sector continues to demand increasing amounts of electricity. The Johor state government had approved 65 data center projects, with 21 already operational, and expected to consume nearly 1.1 GW of electricity, while projects under construction or in the planning stage will require another 4 to 5 GW.

To ensure these new facilities do not affect public electricity supply, the Johor State Data Center Development Coordination Committee (JPPPDNJ) has been established to oversee proposed developments. The committee is chaired by Johor Housing and Local Government Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Jafni Md Shukor, with Lee ing Han, as deputy chairman.

All proposed data centre developments are required to obtain approval from the Committee prior to applying to the local authorities for planning permission. The committee also evaluates the power usage effectiveness (PUE) to ensure that electricity is used efficiently and in compliance with the prescribed regulations.

Lee Ting Han, state Investment, Trade, Consumer Affairs and Human Resources Committee chairman, described the initiative as part of efforts to maintain sufficient electricity supply for industrial and domestic consumers.

“Overall, these projects are expected to raise Johor’s solar generation capacity by about an additional 5 GW by 2030 or 2031 for channeling to data centres and large-scale industries,” Lee Ting Han told reporters on October 25, before the closing ceremony of the JTDC Mega Job Fair at the Tunku Mahkota Ismail Youth Centre in Iskandar Puteri, as per a report by The Edge Malaysia.

Lee also commented on the use of solar power, saying, “These are long-term plans because developing new electricity generation capacity takes a long time. Efforts to increase electricity generation through solar projects, off-grid solutions and new tenders issued by the Energy Commission are being actively pursued by both the Johor government and the federal government. We are confident that this careful planning will ensure an adequate electricity supply to support the growth of the data centre industry and other industrial developments in Johor.”

The Energy Commission, under the Ministry of Energy Transition and Water Transformation, has called for tenders to add 8 GW of capacity across Peninsular Malaysia, with a significant portion expected to be allocated to Johor.

Solar projects with a combined capacity of 4 GW are planned for Kota Tinggi and Mersing, with implementation expected to begin in stages from mid 2029, a separate 1 GW solar project is planned for Segamat.

stories.title: ACE-Market bound MyDCD looks beyond Klang Valley amid data centre building boom
stories.summary: ACE-Market bound MyDCD Bhd is optimistic there is demand for its core engineering services outside the Klang Valley amid a data centre boom across the country.

sources.name: The Edge Malaysia — data centre search

stories.content:
KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 26): ACE-Market bound MyDCD Bhd is optimistic there is demand for its core engineering services outside the Klang Valley amid a data centre boom across the country.

Klang Valley projects made up almost all of the engineering firm's revenue for the financial year ended June 30, 2026 (FY2026).

“We will evaluate opportunities to come about down south or the northern side of Malaysia, we will explore opportunities after the listing,” chief executive officer Chris Ow Yong told reporters at the company's prospectus launch on Monday.

MyDCD, which specialises in integrating mechanical, electrical, plumbing and fire protection (MEPF) systems for critical infrastructure like data centres, has 15 years of experience in the industry.

The group currently serves clients operating enterprise and co-location data centres, with facility sizes ranging from 10MW to 20MW.

Addressing concerns about utility disruptions in data centre developments, Yong said such risks are unlikely to impact its operations and secured order book.

He said the company received projects only from clients that secured utility allocations from the authorities.

As at Sept 30, the group has an order book of RM1.32 billion to be recognised until FY2032.

MyDCD’s main customer is Binastra Builders Sdn Bhd, a wholly owned construction unit of Main Market-listed Binastra Corporation Bhd (KL:BNASTRA). It has a three-year relationship with Binastra Builders, with 85% of MyDCD's FY2026 revenue derived from the firm.

MyDCD's net profit has grown from RM16.8 million in FY2023 to RM66.8 million in FY2026, with a compounded annual growth rate of 58.4%.

However, its profit after tax margin has been narrowing from 11.07% in FY2024 to 10.61% in FY2025 and 10.03% in FY2026. As of end-June, the company has cash and bank balances of RM27.69 million with no borrowings.

The company is scheduled to list on Bursa Malaysia's ACE Market on Nov 17 with IPO applications to close on Nov 2. The exercise is expected to raise RM268.8 million for the company and its shareholders.

stories.content:
BENGALURU (Oct 26): Tata Communications, which offers data connections and cybersecurity to enterprises, announced investments of close to US$450 million on Monday to build high-speed network cables connecting India’s AI data-centre corridors.

The company will build around 10,000 kilometres of new long-haul fiber cables across India.

The project will connect cloud services firms, global capability centres and other organisations such as banks to data-centre clusters.

Expansion will be in three phases: Mumbai-Pune-Hyderabad-Chennai corridor, the east coast and western India data-centre ecosystems, including Vizag, Bhubaneswar, Jamnagar and GIFT City.

stories.title: IJM said to have bagged K2 data centre construction job
stories.summary: Summary • IJM is likely to secure a RM500 million contract for the construction of a data centre for K2 Strategic Infrastructure ...

sources.name: The Edge Malaysia — data centre search

stories.content:
This article first appeared in The Edge Malaysia Weekly on October 19, 2026 - October 25, 2026

Construction giant IJM Corp Bhd (KL:IJM) is understood to have emerged as the front runner to win a contract worth about RM500 million to build a data centre for K2 Strategic Infrastructure Malaysia Sdn Bhd, a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Kuok group, in Johor, sources familiar with the matter tell The Edge.

While details are scarce, two separate sources confirmed that the K2 contract is a done deal. One says, “It’s in the bag, it’s a matter of time before it’s announced.” The other source says IJM beat a number of companies to secure the contract, and that an announcement could be made as early as this week, if it all pans out.

IJM executives could not be contacted for comment after office hours last Friday.

K2, a turnkey provider of hyperscale data centre campuses, has two existing data centres in Kulai, Johor, namely JHR04 and JHR01-03, with a capacity of 234mw designed capacity. Other than in Johor, K2 also has four data centres in Dublin, Ireland, one in Cikarang Indonesia, and another in Rayong, Thailand.

A leader in the global data centre industry, it is run by managing director and CEO Kuok Meng Wei, the 42-year-old grandson of billionaire tycoon, Robert Kuok Hock Nien, who turned 103 earlier this month.

According to news reports, Meng Wei’s mandate is to grow K2’s capacity to 1,200mw by 2030, marking a tenfold increase from current levels.

On its website, K2 says it has 114mw capacity in operation, 82mw capacity under construction and about 350mw deemed to be in the “pre-construction project phase”.

IJM appears to be on a roll, with its construction arm securing a number of new contracts lately. Other businesses under IJM’s belt include property development, port operations, toll road concessions, manufacturing and quarrying.

It is worth noting that only last week, IJM secured a RM1.23 billion contract from AT&S Austria Technologie & Systemtechnik (Malaysia) Sdn Bhd to construct semiconductor manufacturing facilities at the Kulim Hi-Tech Park in Kedah. The Austrian contract came on the back of more than RM900 million in jobs for semiconductor and medical technology projects, secured since August 2026.

Another noteworthy contract secured in April is a RM658 million agreement with Sime Darby Property Bhd (KL:SIMEPROP) for the construction of a hyperscale data centre in Elmina Business Park, Selangor.

When IJM announces the half-a-billion ringgit K2 data centre construction contract, its existing construction order book will swell to more than RM11 billion, with its current year order book replenishment at RM3.5 billion.

The company’s construction tender book is at about RM18 billion, and includes the Penang airport expansion and a RM1 billion civil servant housing project in Nusantara, Indonesia, among others.

IJM could get more aggressive in replenishing its order book in the next few months, given plans to float its construction arm early next year.

For its first financial quarter ended June 30, 2026, IJM chalked up a net profit of RM137.4 million on the back of RM2.29 billion in revenue. For the corresponding period a year ago, IJM registered a net profit of RM95.6 million on revenue of RM1.73 billion.

In the notes accompanying its financial statement, IJM says the better showing was driven primarily by the construction division, among others.

On its prospects for the financial year ending March 31, 2027, IJM says, “The construction division is expected to perform strongly in FY2027 underpinned by its strong order book of RM14.5 billion (including our share from joint ventures and associates) comprising hyperscale data centres, advanced manufacturing and warehousing facilities and road infrastructure projects … the group is confident it will perform better operationally this financial year.”

As at end-June this year, IJM had deposits, cash and bank balances of RM2.26 billion while on the other side of the balance sheet the company had short-term debt commitments of RM2.48 billion and long-term borrowings of RM1.25 billion. It is noteworthy that IJM had retained profits of RM4.11 billion.

IJM’s net cash flow from operating activities was RM353 million for the three months ended June 2026.
